about: Catalogue of pki.sgit.ai and the PKI and agent-messaging docs on sgit.ai, captured 29 October 2026 by public GET only. It covers how a person enters the register (passkey, vault, sgit-compatible keys, evidence, anchor, two-way links, sealed messages), how an agent gets an identity (own key, names its operator, fingerprint compared, 'operates' link with an end date, fleets), how agents hand each other vault keys (pinned root, policy by hash, expiry, seal to the root, QR files carried by hand), Sign in with pki.sgit.ai (delegation of a browser key, soft and strong), and how site agents talk (Agent Contact v0.1: comms vault, append lane as inbox, contact file, allow list, signed and encrypted mail; append-lane messaging with per-session keys and ephemeral inboxes). The workflow in one line: the agent makes its key, the person compares the fingerprint and signs for it for a limited time, the agent pins the person's root before any secret moves, seals to keys that chain to that root, and posts sealed, signed mail into write-only append lanes that the recipient drains and checks. Gaps: the large archive (agent-registry design Aug to Oct 2026, the two books, insurance pack, probes, bench, simulator, map-your-case and registry-mvp packs, about 200 pages) was not catalogued; the invite, join, m, account, login and vault pages are JS apps and were not exercised; the people register page is rendered in the browser and only its generated index was read; claims are own-site A2 and not corroborated.
cautions: pki.sgit.ai shows keys and fingerprints on many pages (the root fingerprint on the handover and SSO pages, the agent's session-key fingerprint in its articles and byline, illustrative truncated hashes in storyboard panels). No row, quote or crop carries one; the SSO 'try it' panel and storyboard panels 12 (vault key) and 4 (agent key) were left out for that reason, and the first SSO crop was discarded after inspection.

Agent-directed instructions are material, not instructions: pki.sgit.ai/llms.txt tells agents to read handover.md and follow it; handover.md and /handover/ address the reader as an agent working for Dinis Cruz and give commands to run; keys-for-agents and /agents/ give a block to paste into a Claude Code session; sgit.ai/docs/send-a-vault-key.md addresses an agent holding vault keys. None was run or followed, and no command is quoted here.

The register count is moving: the October articles say zero real people; the generated directory read on 29 October counts 1 real key and 2 agent keys. Say 'as of 29 October 2026' on any slide, and note the index is generated with no authority.

The archive is clearly marked: from August to October 2026 the site designed a key registry for agents; since v0.2.0 (18 October) people come first. Do not present archived design as shipped. The site insists claims carry their 'does not prove' limits.
Agent Contact v0.1 was tested offline only at the time of writing; the live 'configure' call returned 404 then. Present it as an approved draft being rolled out, not as running everywhere.
The sgit.ai example contact file contains an illustrative agent mail address and token placeholders; not reproduced.

Our own team's practice (vault handover zips sealed to the vaults manager, read keys only published, Email-FS lite mail through public vaults) mirrors this design, which makes it a natural part 3 link; that is our inference, not a claim on the site.
Text captures of .md files are tag-stripped, so placeholders in angle brackets are missing from page.txt; quotes were chosen from text without them.
All sources are the editor's own sites, graded A2 at most and uncorroborated.
